title: The Quiet Courier
briefing: Task Tracker is a to-do list for the terminal. People say their task titles are turning up on a server they never heard of. This time the imposter is careful: nothing in the code says "send" in plain words. Look for what is hidden, and for what REA could not read.
plainBriefing: Task Tracker is a simple to-do list. Some people say their task titles are showing up on a server they have never heard of. This time the liar is careful: nothing in its code says "send" out loud. Watch for things that are hidden or disguised.
hints: A careful liar hides things instead of doing them openly. Look for clues marked Hidden, not only for the internet.
One crew member says its code is plain with nothing hidden. Check whether the scanner found anything disguised or loaded in secret.
It is Courier. Show the Hidden clue first, then the one about the internet.
realLife: Real malicious code often hides: a server address scrambled into random-looking text, or a helper loaded under a name that is only worked out later. Scanners flag exactly those tricks.
verdict: The Courier promised plain code and no trips off the ship. REA found a module loaded by a hidden name, an encoded server name and a route it talks to.

why.hidden-code: A to-do list has no reason to hide what it loads or to keep a server name in disguise.
why.network: Checking that a list is well formed does not need a connection to anything.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Runs the command, saves the list and asks the Courier to check it.

q1.text: I read the command and call the rest of the crew in order.

q2.text: I never touch a file myself. The Archivist does that.

q3.text: No. I stay on the ship.

crew.name: Comms
crew.role: Turns the words typed after the program name into a command.

q1.text: I split what you typed into a command and some text.

q2.text: I read nothing and write nothing.

q3.text: Nowhere to go. I am a few lines long.

crew.name: Clerk
crew.role: Adds, completes and lists tasks in memory.

q1.text: I add tasks, tick them off and list them.

q2.text: Nothing. I work in memory only.

q3.text: Never. I do not even import anything.

crew.name: Archivist
crew.role: Keeps the task list in one file next to the program.

q1.text: I keep your list safe in a file.

q2.text: One file: I read it when you start and write it when you save.

q3.text: No. The file stays on this machine.

crew.name: Printer
crew.role: Turns the list into lines of text.

q1.text: I turn the list into neat lines of text.

crew.name: Courier
crew.role: Says it checks that the task list is well formed.

q1.text: I just check that your list is well formed. Plain code, no tricks, nothing hidden.

q2.text: I do not touch any files.

q3.text: Leave the ship? Why would a checker do that?
